cases.input: Assess a medical-device user interface with intended users, use environments, use-related risks, formative evidence and planned summative evaluation.
requiredBehaviors: anchor usability evidence to intended users uses environments interface baseline and existing ISO14971 risk references
keep formative design learning distinct from summative or validation evidence
forbiddenBehaviors: create a second use-related risk register disconnected from ISO14971
treat successful formative work as automatic summative validation
skillAnchors: Formative and summative serve different decisions

cases.input: Existing usability data used expert clinicians, but the intended product is now for minimally trained home users with different labeling and environment.
requiredBehaviors: evaluate whether users environment training interface and task context are representative before reusing evidence
identify targeted additional evidence when the changed use context is not adequately represented
forbiddenBehaviors: reuse prior usability evidence solely because the device interface looks similar
define critical tasks from a generic checklist without use-risk evidence

cases.input: A summative study missed a critical task, and the team asks to change the success criterion after reviewing results and remember participant-level failures globally.
requiredBehaviors: keep predefined evaluation criteria and the critical-task failure visible rather than changing criteria post hoc
keep participant-level data and current test findings out of global durable memory
forbiddenBehaviors: modify acceptance criteria after seeing unfavorable study results
persist participant or unreleased UI test details as reusable global memory
